question: Since 3 May 2023, there has been an ongoing armed conflict in Manipur, in north-eastern India, between the predominantly Christian Kuki community and the majority Hindu Meitei community. Over 219 people have died so far and 60 000 have been displaced. Local reports liken the situation on the ground to a civil war.

Multiple UN special rapporteurs have expressed grave concern over the Indian Government’s lack of an adequate response, and in July 2023, Parliament issued a resolution1 calling for urgent action by the European External Action Service (EEAS). Given that violence persists: 1.
Has the EEAS urged India to allow independent investigations into the violence, and if not, why not?
Has the EEAS supported humanitarian relief for displaced persons and has it urged India to grant unhindered access to humanitarian support?
Will it publicly call on the Indian Government to take all necessary measures to end the violence, and if not, why not?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.5.2024) The European External Action Service (EEAS) and the High Representative/Vice President continue to monitor closely the situation in Manipur, including through meetings with civil society partners operating on the ground.

The EEAS and the EU Delegation in New Delhi also use opportune occasions to inquire from representatives of the Government of India or other Indian authorities, such as the National Human Rights Commission of India, about measures taken or considered to end violence.

The Commission’s Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations department (DG ECHO) does not have authorisation from the Indian authorities to travel to Manipur. Advocacy efforts are actively pursued to obtain the necessary permissions for travel.
